evidence.quote: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:livid|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)leh₃y-}} From {{inh|en|enm|livid}}, {{m|enm|livide}}, from {{der|en|fro|livide}}, from {{der|en|la|līvidus||bluish, livid; envious}}, from {{m|la|līveō||be of a bluish color or livid; envy}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*sliwēō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sliwo-}}, suffixed form of {{m|ine-pro|*(s)leh₃y-||bluish}}. See also {{cog|ang|slā||sloe}}, {{cog|cy|lliw||splendor, color}}, {{cog|sga|li}}, {{cog|lt|slyvas||plum}}, and {{cog|ru|-}} and {{cog|cu|-}} {{m|ru|слива||plum}}.
"of a bluish-leaden color," from Old French livide (13c.) and directly from Latin lividus… See origin and meaning of livid. from Old French livide (13c.
